Chain Rule 10: Radical Trigonometric Sine Function

Course: Mathematics-I (Differential Calculus) Textbook Page: 32 | Problem: 10
প্রদত্ত সমীকরণ: y=sin⁡xy = \sqrt{\sin x}y=sinx​
নির্ণেয়: dydx\dfrac{dy}{dx}dxdy​
📘 English Note — Radical Trigonometric Chain Rule Formulation
The problem is a composite radical-trigonometric function: y=f(g(x)),where f(u)=u,  u=g(x)=sin⁡xy = f(g(x)), \quad \text{where } f(u) = \sqrt{u}, \; u = g(x) = \sin xy=f(g(x)),where f(u)=u​,u=g(x)=sinx Applying Leibniz's Chain Rule: dydx=ddu(u)⋅dudx=12u⋅ddx(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x2sin⁡x\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{du}(\sqrt{u}) \cdot \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \frac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}dxdy​=dud​(u​)⋅dxdu​=2u​1​⋅dxd​(sinx)=2sinx​cosx​
১. গাণিতিক কাঠামো ও প্রয়োজনীয় সূত্রসমূহ
উপাদান (Component) ফাংশন রূপ প্রমিত সূত্র (Standard Derivative)
বহিঃস্থ বর্গমূল ফাংশন (Outer Radical) u\sqrt{u}u​ ddu(u)=12u\frac{d}{du}(\sqrt{u}) = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}dud​(u​)=2u​1​
অভ্যন্তরীণ সাইন ফাংশন (Inner Core) u=sin⁡xu = \sin xu=sinx dudx=ddx(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x\frac{du}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos xdxdu​=dxd​(sinx)=cosx
সম্মিলিত চেইন রুল sin⁡x\sqrt{\sin x}sinx​ dydx=cos⁡x2sin⁡x\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}dxdy​=2sinx​cosx​
২. ধাপে ধাপে পূর্ণাঙ্গ গাণিতিক সমাধান
ধাপ ১:

dydx=ddx[sin⁡x]\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx}\left[\sqrt{\sin x}\right]dxdy​=dxd​[sinx​]
ধাপ ২:

dydx=12sin⁡x⋅ddx(sin⁡x)\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\sin x}} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}(\sin x)dxdy​=2sinx​1​⋅dxd​(sinx)
ধাপ ৩:

Chain Rule 10: Engineering & Rigorous Analysis

Course: Mathematics-I (Differential Calculus) Theoretical Foundations & Examination Blueprint
⚠️ English Note — Critical AMIE Exam Traps & Pitfalls
  • Trap 1 (Incomplete Radical Differentiation): Writing only 12sin⁡x\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}2sinx​1​ without multiplying by the inner derivative ddx(sin⁡x)=cos⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos xdxd​(sinx)=cosx.
  • Trap 2 (Sign Error on Sine Derivative): Ensure ddx(sin⁡x)=+cos⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = +\cos xdxd​(sinx)=+cosx. Do not confuse it with ddx(cos⁡x)=−sin⁡x\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin xdxd​(cosx)=−sinx.
  • Trap 3 (Division by Zero at Nodal Points): Note that when sin⁡x=0\sin x = 0sinx=0 (at x=kπx = k\pix=kπ), the derivative is singular (vertical tangents).
🟣 English Note — Domain, Non-Negativity & Boundary Regularity (AMIE Rigor)
  • Function Domain: For real sin⁡x\sqrt{\sin x}sinx​, the radicand must be non-negative: sin⁡x≥0  ⟹  x∈[2kπ,(2k+1)π],  k∈Z\sin x \ge 0 \implies x \in [2k\pi, (2k+1)\pi], \; k \in \mathbb{Z}sinx≥0⟹x∈[2kπ,(2k+1)π],k∈Z
  • Differentiability Domain (Open Intervals): Since the derivative places sin⁡x\sqrt{\sin x}sinx​ in the denominator, sin⁡x≠0\sin x \neq 0sinx=0: Dom(dydx)=⋃k∈Z(2kπ,(2k+1)π)\text{Dom}\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) = \bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{Z}} (2k\pi, (2k+1)\pi)Dom(dxdy​)=k∈Z⋃​(2kπ,(2k+1)π)
  • Vertical Tangents: At boundary points x→kπx \to k\pix→kπ, lim⁡∣dydx∣=∞\lim \left|\frac{dy}{dx}\right| = \inftylim​dxdy​​=∞, representing infinite slopes.
💡 English Note — Substitution & Power Rule Proofs
Method A (Leibniz Substitution): Let u=sin⁡x  ⟹  dudx=cos⁡xu = \sin x \implies \frac{du}{dx} = \cos xu=sinx⟹dxdu​=cosx. Then y=u  ⟹  dydu=12uy = \sqrt{u} \implies \frac{dy}{du} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}y=u​⟹dudy​=2u​1​. dydx=dydu⋅dudx=12sin⁡x⋅cos⁡x=cos⁡x2sin⁡x\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dy}{du} \cdot \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\sin x}} \cdot \cos x = \frac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}dxdy​=dudy​⋅dxdu​=2sinx​1​⋅cosx=2sinx​cosx​ Method B (Fractional Exponent Power Rule): y=(sin⁡x)12  ⟹  dydx=12(sin⁡x)−12⋅cos⁡x=cos⁡x2sin⁡xy = (\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2}} \implies \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1}{2}(\sin x)^{-\frac{1}{2}} \cdot \cos x = \frac{\cos x}{2\sqrt{\sin x}}y=(sinx)21​⟹dxdy​=21​(sinx)−21​⋅cosx=2sinx​cosx​
